items.title: Tech stocks today: SpaceX lockup ends, Google faces AI leadership shakeup
items.summary: Tech stocks coverage for the week of Aug. 3.

items.title: What the bond market is signaling for SpaceX's hopes to ramp up debt sales
items.summary: Wellington Management fixed income portfolio manager Brij Khurana weighs in on what the bond market (^TYX, ^TNX, ^FVX) could be signaling about SpaceX's (SPCX) debt sales plans, especially as shares of Elon Musk's space venture continue to slide lower.

items.title: Why Google's AI leadership shake-up isn't a good look
items.summary: Yahoo Finance Technology Editor Dan Howley chats with Morning Brief host Julie Hyman about Google's (GOOG, GOOGL) recently announced AI leadership changes.

items.title: Michael Burry Shares 'Three Great Charts' That Show Big AI Capex Could Unwind As Badly As Housing Did In 2008
items.summary: Cloud companies’ capex would run at roughly 3% of the U.S. GDP every year from 2027 to 2029, up from 0.3% of GDP in 2019 and 1.4% in 2025, according to a top economist.

items.title: What Block (SQ)'s Buyback Completion And Google AI Tie-Up Means For Shareholders
items.summary: In early August 2026, Block reported second-quarter revenue of US$6,617.69 million with net income of US$88.52 million, while also completing a multi-year US$4.43 billion share repurchase program that retired 11.03% of its stock. A day later, Google announced an expanded collaboration with Square that plugs food and beverage sellers directly into Ask Maps and Order by Cash App, tying Block’s payments ecosystems more tightly into everyday AI-driven restaurant discovery and ordering. items.title: Is Broadcom the Best Chip Stock to Own Now? Maybe
items.summary: Broadcom sits at a tollbooth on the AI buildout, and one look at its order book raises a question worth asking: why are so many chip investors still looking elsewhere?

items.title: Alphabet and Tesla: A Single Divergence Tells Us So Much About Current Reality
items.summary: Alphabet and Tesla both reported earnings the same day, both burned billions on AI, and both are chasing the same future. So why did the market punish one and reward the other?

items.title: Earnings Have Been Excellent. Why Stocks Aren’t Showing It.
items.summary: A mix of high expectations, profit-taking, and a slight dip in valuations has sent S&P 500 stocks sputtering even after solid earnings reports.
